angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 653,958 km at 45.74 pc = 0.19 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 21.8623 +/- 0.0164 mas (same row, RUWE 0.95): 45.74 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.94 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1860 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract): 653,958 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.99 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1860 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5752 +/- 100 K from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1860 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1860 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1860.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.487, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
